summary: The note describes how local retailers have adopted augmented reality (AR) since around September 2023 to blend online convenience with in-store experience. It covers pioneering stores, a study showing higher customer retention, the VisionAR platform that lowers costs, and real-world uses in pet and garden shops. It argues AR boosts sales, reduces returns, creates tech jobs and strengthens local economies, with growth expected ahead.
one_line: Local retailers are adopting augmented reality to offer try-before-you-buy shopping, boosting engagement, sales and retention and strengthening the local economy since September 2023.
key_facts: Local retailers have been integrating augmented reality (AR) into shopping since around September 10, 2023, blurring the lines between online and in-store shopping.
Emma’s Boutique and The Modern Man Store were pioneers, rolling out AR apps for virtually trying on clothes or seeing how furniture looks in homes.
A Local Economic Development Center study published October 15, 2023 noted a 20% increase in customer retention for stores using AR compared to those that did not.
Sarah Johnson, a 29-year-old teacher, said AR changed her shopping habits because she can see items on her or in her space before buying online.
Local tech startup VisionAR introduced a cost-effective AR platform for local retailers on October 20, 2023.
VisionAR CEO Marcus Thompson said the goal is to 'democratize AR for all retailers' so they can offer experiences once possible only for large corporations.
Pet Shop Corner launched an AR feature on November 5, 2023 that lets pet owners visualize pet accessories on their pets.
GreenThumb Nurseries introduced an AR app that lets gardeners design gardens and test plant arrangements before purchasing.
Local stores report that AR has led to a decrease in returns because customers make more informed purchase decisions.
Chamber of Commerce spokesperson Andrew Liu said on November 30, 2023 that AR adoption has driven sales and sparked synergy between technology providers and retailers.
AR is creating new tech-sector jobs to deploy and maintain AR systems for retail.

Retail experts predict future AR enhancements such as personalized product recommendations and social media integration for shared shopping, and AR app data gives retailers insight into consumer preferences.
